messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Eversource Health (dedicated VPC) — elevated 5xx rate on inference pool e-hr-vpc-02, started 12:42 UTC. Alerts: request errors, degraded token throughput. Paging oncall. Logs attached: /alerts/3345001234
Mia (oncall): saw it. I'm on it. preliminary from metrics: tail latency spikes and KV cache eviction rate up ~8x. Looks like model kv hotspoting from long-chat sessions.
Javier: 12:44 — adding context: this tenant pins to model redwood-2-large-ep16 in dedicated pool. That model has larger KV footprint; combined with a burst of long histories caused memory pressure -> eviction thrash -> increased CPU on runtime -> 5xx.
Samira (sre): oncall handoff: Mia, do we have capacity to move to ephemeral safe variant? Or fall back to smaller model copy in same pool? We need to avoid cross-tenant noisy-neighboring of other customers.
Mia (oncall): propose immediate mitigation: pin tenant to safe variant redwood-2-medium-q8 on a different node group with reserved KV. Steps:
- apply tenant override: tenant_config.set_override(tenant_id=E-HLTH-001, model="redwood-2-medium-q8", rollout=100%)
- re-route traffic to pool e-hr-vpc-03 (less loaded)
- enable KV prefix caching for the tenant
If IaC needed, I'll run the command via ops-run.
Nora (cs): I'm in the thread — telling customer that we're investigating and may migrate to a verified fallback for a short window. Need ETA and customer impact notes for support ticket.
Tyler (cust-success): quick note: Eversource SLOs are strict; they requested zero functional regression. Anything we do must preserve semantics — medium model is verified on baseline tests but may change latency/quality slightly. We'll need to offer a post-mortem and rollback window.
Alex (engineer): quick check: redwood-2-medium-q8 has been validated as a safevariant for enterprise tenants; perf benchmarks show <3% relative regression on our evaluation prompts and much lower memory usage. It's available as compatible architecture (no tokenizer mismatch).
DevOps-bot: candidate nodes in e-hr-vpc-03: node-77, node-80, node-83. Current free GPU slots: 12. Estimated time to drain and warm KV: ~45s for canary, ~3m for 100%.
Samira (sre): plan:
1) Canary 10% traffic to redwood-2-medium-q8 on node-77. Monitor 5xx and tail latency 1m.
2) If stable for 2m, escalate to 50% and move to nodes 80/83 for capacity.
3) Full 100% reroute and remove tenant pin after 30m of stable metrics.
I will own the execution and keep Mia as escalation.
Mia (oncall): executing canary now. Running tenant override script:
```
ops-run tenant-override --tenant E-HLTH-001 --model redwood-2-medium-q8 --pool e-hr-vpc-03 --percent 10
```
Mia (oncall): 12:48 — canary hit. Initial telemetry: 5xx rate down 60% for canary requests, p95 latency down 30%. Some variance in generation length but no crash signatures.
Javier: checking logs for hot loops. There are still a few eviction peaks from older nodes. Recommend we also bump kv_cache_size for tenant to 1.5x default while pinned. Mia, can you apply:
```
ops-config set tenant/E-HLTH-001/kv_cache_multiplier 1.5
```
Mia (oncall): applied kv cache multiplier. Monitoring.
Nora (cs): drafting message to customer: "We are routing a small portion of your traffic to a verified fallback model to stabilize latency and error rates. This is temporary; we'll keep you updated and perform a thorough post-incident review." Want to include expected rollback timeline (30–90 minutes).
Tyler (cust-success): agrees. Please cc compliance if any logs are shifted. Eversource may ask for redaction of certain logs — keep them on private plane.
Samira (sre): 12:52 — promoting to 50% now.
DevOps-bot: promotion command executed. New traffic split: 50% redwood-2-medium-q8 (node-77/80) / 50% original.
Mia (oncall): metrics: overall cluster error rate down 45% and p99 latency recovering. No new alerts.
Alex (engineer): Also toggled safevariant-config to prevent auto-upgrades for this tenant while under override. Command:
```
tenant-lock --tenant E-HLTH-001 --prevent-auto-upgrade true
```
Samira (sre): after 12:58 of stable metrics, we should do a full 100% cutover. If at any point model quality regress >5% on eval set we rollback.
Mia (oncall): cutting to 100% now.
DevOps-bot: complete — tenant traffic moved to redwood-2-medium-q8 on e-hr-vpc-03.
Mia (oncall): 13:01 — 100% migration done. Error rates back to baseline, tail latencies acceptable. Recording incident mitigation steps in runbook.
Nora (cs): letting customer know migration completed and that we will validate logs for functional regressions. Offering to run side-by-side prompts with their key flows.
Tyler (cust-success): schedule post-mortem and quality audit. Also propose next steps for permanent fix: either reduce default conversation length, increase dedicated KV sizing, or offer alternate model with same quality but lower KV (redwood-2-large-q4f16?).
Javier: long-term remediation: implement tenant-specific KV sizing policy and burst isolation windows for long-history sessions. Also evaluate memory-aware scheduler to prevent co-locating heavy KV tenants on same node.
Samira (sre): I'll create a follow-up ticket for infra changes and link tenant incident. Also note: we temporarily disabled automatic fallthrough to hosted fallback for this tenant to honor enterprise isolation policy.
Mia (oncall): handing off to night oncall (Samira) at 19:00 UTC. Samira will own monitoring and the rollback window. Leaving incident status: mitigated, customer notified, post-mortem pending.
Nora (cs): ack. I'll coordinate the customer-facing post-mortem and will include timeline + traffic shifts.
Alex (engineer): one more note — we captured KV cache evictions and will attach sample logs to the post-mortem for model engineering. Potential optimization: K/V affinity heuristics in runtime v2.3.
Tyler (cust-success): thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the customer and schedule a 1:1 for remediation discussion.
Mia (oncall): closing the immediate pager. If anything flares, ping with @here and set high priority. :thumbsup:
